key_insight: ShipNet uses geometric deep learning on hull point clouds to rapidly predict both local pressure and far-field wave patterns from ship geometry and speed.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate enables fast hydrodynamic evaluation for ship design exploration, cutting turnaround time from expensive potential-flow simulation to near real-time inference.
method: Regularized dynamic graph convolutional backbone on hull point clouds
Multi-head decoder for hull pressure and free-surface elevation
Composite loss with point-wise regression and image-structure terms
evidence_signal: Trained on 420 inviscid free-surface panel simulations from two parent yacht hulls, the model achieved R^2=0.98 for pressure and R^2=0.91 for wave fields, with about 0.15 s inference per case.
watch_item: Generalization is limited by the narrow geometry and speed ranges and by training on inviscid rather than viscous flow data.
paper_title: ShipNet: A Geometric Deep Learning Surrogate for Real-Time Ship Hydrodynamics
